fractional-ownership-vs-timeshare.title: Fractional Ownership vs Timeshare: What You Actually Own
fractional-ownership-vs-timeshare.subtitle: Two products with similar surface appeal and fundamentally different fundamentals. The deeded-asset / right-to-use distinction is the whole game.
fractional-ownership-vs-timeshare.metaDescription: One is a deeded share of real property you can sell. The other is a contract to use a week. Compared on cost, exit, appreciation and title.

fractional-ownership-vs-second-home.title: Fractional Ownership vs Buying a Second Home Outright
fractional-ownership-vs-second-home.h1: Fractional Ownership vs Buying a Second Home Outright
fractional-ownership-vs-second-home.subtitle: The strongest buyer objection: "Why not just buy it all?" The honest answer depends on how many days a year you'll actually use the property and how the capital you don't tie up could be working elsewhere.
fractional-ownership-vs-second-home.metaDescription: The whole house costs eight times as much and most owners use it six weeks. Compared on purchase price, running costs and what happens when you sell.

pacaso-vs-myne.title: Pacaso vs MYNE: Co-Ownership Operators Compared
pacaso-vs-myne.subtitle: Two of the most prominent fractional co-ownership operators, with very different geographic strengths, operational models, and buyer profiles.
pacaso-vs-myne.metaDescription: Compared side by side: share prices, nights a year, running costs, booking rules and how each one handles resale. Updated September 2026.

pacaso-vs-vivla.title: Pacaso vs Vivla: Co-Ownership Operators Compared
pacaso-vs-vivla.subtitle: Pacaso brings the largest cross-border footprint in fractional co-ownership; Vivla goes deeper in Spain than anyone. They serve different buyers — sometimes the same buyer at different moments.
pacaso-vs-vivla.metaDescription: One sells across the US and Europe, one only in Spain. Share prices, nights, running costs, booking and resale, side by side. Updated September 2026.

myne-vs-vivla.title: MYNE vs Vivla: Co-Ownership Operators Compared
myne-vs-vivla.subtitle: Two European-headquartered fractional operators with overlapping Spanish footprints and very different philosophies. MYNE goes broad across nine countries; Vivla goes deep in one.
myne-vs-vivla.metaDescription: Both sell eighths of European holiday homes. Compared on share price, nights a year, running costs, booking rules and resale. Updated September 2026.

cop-vs-going-direct.title: Buying Through an Agent vs Going Direct to the Operator
cop-vs-going-direct.h1: Through Co-Ownership Property, or straight to the operator?
cop-vs-going-direct.subtitle: The share costs the same either way. What changes is what you can see before you commit, and who you can ask when the answer is inconvenient.
cop-vs-going-direct.metaDescription: The share price is identical either way — the operator pays the commission, not you. What differs is the comparison, the running costs you see, and who answers.

best-fractional-ownership-companies.title: The Best Fractional Ownership Companies in 2026, Compared
best-fractional-ownership-companies.h1: The best fractional ownership companies in 2026
best-fractional-ownership-companies.subtitle: Six operators, 268 live homes, and the figures measured from the listings themselves rather than taken from anybody's marketing — including the running costs two of them publish and four do not.
best-fractional-ownership-companies.metaDescription: Pacaso, MYNE, Vivla, &Hamlet, Abitaro and Paris Property Group compared on price, running costs, nights and resale — measured across 268 live homes.

pacaso-alternatives.title: Pacaso Alternatives: Four Reasons, Four Different Answers
pacaso-alternatives.subtitle: People look for one for four reasons — price, geography, letting, or wanting the running costs up front — and each has a different answer.
pacaso-alternatives.metaDescription: Too expensive, not in Europe, want to let it, or want Paris? Each reason has a different answer. Compared on measured figures from 268 live homes.
